  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup red-check route (`if [ "${PR_CHECKS_LAST_PENDING:-0}" = "0" ] && [ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURE_NAMES_FILE}" ]; then`) only runs when the snapshot-derived failure-names file is non-empty. `_pr_checks_completed` has already confirmed `reason=blocking` with pending=0. When the snapshot is disabled (CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=false sentinel), missing, for another head or failed to render, a settled red required check skips `rb_judge_route_red_checks merge_with_followup`.
  WHY: The judge falls through to `judge_skip_reason=blocking_check_runs` (line 4127) with no final-CI repair request, dispatch, hand-over, ai:needs-human or ERROR alert. Stall recovery re-fires the judge into the same branch on every round, which is the #9679/#10063 stall the issue set out to remove. The guard is also inconsistent with `rb_judge_manual_merge_red_check`, which accepts `[ -s names ] || [ -s section ]`. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR, mapped here to high.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  EVIDENCE: The block calls `rb_judge_route_red_checks merge_with_followup`, but its condition requires `[ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURE_NAMES_FILE}" ]`. No branch writes the names file when the check-run snapshot is disabled, unavailable or for another head, so on that path the run keeps the pre-#10063 `blocking_check_runs` behaviour. The manual-merge paths were fixed for the same cases in an earlier run.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:line 4115, in the merge_with_followup refusal branch: `if [ "${PR_CHECKS_LAST_PENDING:-0}" = "0" ] && [ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURE_NAMES_FILE}" ]; then RB_MERGE_STATUS="checks_failed"; rb_judge_route_red_checks merge_with_followup || true ...` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The branch runs only after `_pr_checks_completed` (lines 4094-4101) returned blocking. Per scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:679-683, blocking with pending=0 is always a settled required failure. The extra names-file check skips routing whenever `render_review_rb_ci_failures_file` leaves that file empty: missing snapshot, another head, render failure, or the disabled sentinel (scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:664-673 when CHECK_RUNS_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=false). The same class of gap was already fixed in `rb_judge_manual_merge_red_check` (line 2069, `[ -s names ] || [ -s section ]`), but not here.
  WHY: The judge posts `judge_skip_reason=blocking_check_runs` and the PR stays ai:review-blocked. Stall recovery re-fires the judge into the same branch on every round, with no final-CI repair request, hand-over, ai:needs-human or ERROR alert. This is the PR #9679 stall, now on the merge_with_followup path. Minimal fix: drop the `&& [ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURE_NAMES_FILE}" ]` condition, or widen it to `{ [ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURE_NAMES_FILE}" ] || [ -s "${RB_JUDGE_CI_FAILURES_FILE}" ]; }`.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE, apart from the finding above. That finding breaks the issue goal "With a required check red on the head, the judge's merge is not accepted as the outcome. The run instead takes the final-CI repair path" for merge_with_followup.
